summary: The note describes Lion Island, a river island at the mouth of the Hawkesbury River inside Broken Bay in New South Wales, Australia. It states the island is considered part of a unit whose name was cut off in the clipped text. The name is descriptive, because the island resembles a Sphinx, a mythical crouching lion figure.
one_line: Lion Island is a river island at the Hawkesbury River mouth in Broken Bay, New South Wales, Australia, named for its resemblance to a sphinx.
key_facts: Lion Island is a river island located at the mouth of the Hawkesbury River.
Lion Island is located inside Broken Bay.
Lion Island is in the state of New South Wales, Australia.
The island is considered part of a larger unit, though the name of that unit is missing from the note.
The name Lion Island is a descriptive name.
The island's name reflects that it resembles a Sphinx.
A Sphinx is a mythical figure of a crouching lion.
